definition: Keeping each currency flat so revaluations of assets, liabilities and FX deals cancel out in P&L. No hedge accounting is needed.
example: TRS holds EUR 40m of IC loans and sells EUR 40m forward: a EUR move changes both by the same amount.

definition: A treasury entity that acts as the bank for the group: entities deposit surplus cash, borrow and deal FX with it, and settle through intercompany current accounts.
example: MGT pays payroll from its account; TRS funds the account the same day and books the amount on MGT's IC current account.

definition: A fund investing in short-term, high-quality debt. Used for surplus cash with same-day access. Interest accrues daily and is paid early the next month.
example: USD 60m in MMF-USD-A at 4.2% earns about USD 7,000 a day (actual/360).

definition: A spot (near leg) and a forward (far leg) in opposite directions. Funds one currency from another for a period without changing the FX position.
example: Swap USD 30m into EUR for one month to pay a capital call before a EUR distribution arrives.

definition: Value of an FX forward today: notional times the difference between today's forward rate for the same date and the deal rate, without discounting to today.
example: Bought EUR 10m at 1.0800; today's forward is 1.0850: MTM = +USD 50,000.

definition: Three forecast cases. Base is the expected case; downside is the cash-negative one (calls earlier, distributions later); upside is the cash-positive one.
example: Downside: a USD 40m call lands in week 3 instead of week 8.

definition: Cash and liquid investments plus undrawn committed facilities, minus the cash that must stay put (here the IV buffer).
Intercompany rates set as if the entities were unrelated, so tax authorities accept them. Here: MMF rate + 50 bp when TRS lends, MMF rate - 10 bp when TRS borrows.
The difference between the forward and the spot rate. They come from the interest rate difference between the two currencies over the period (covered interest parity).
example: If USD rates are higher than EUR rates, EUR/USD forward points are positive.

definition: A weekly cash forecast for the next 13 weeks, updated every week: one week is added at the end as one closes.
The maximum that can be drawn on a secured facility: the value of the collateral times the advance rate.
example: IV NAV USD 900m x 25% advance rate = USD 225m available on the secured line.

definition: A loan to an investment vehicle secured on the value of its investments (its NAV).
A fee on the undrawn part of a committed facility, often a share of the margin.
example: 35% x 200 bp = 70 bp a year on the undrawn RCF.

definition: A periodic run (often monthly) that nets intercompany invoices between many entities so each one pays or receives one net amount.
IFRS 9 treatment for hedges of forecast flows: the effective part of the hedge's MTM is held in OCI until the hedged flow reaches P&L.
Hedging the value of a foreign subsidiary's net assets; gains and losses go to the translation reserve in equity.
Discounting future cash flows (for example an FX forward's settlement) with overnight index swap rates to get a present value.
Balances in several accounts are added up for interest without moving cash between them.
A bank regulatory rule: high-quality liquid assets must cover 30 days of stressed outflows.
